REFERENCE ASSIGNMENT — DO NOT SWAP:
IMAGE 1 / STARTER FRAME 0 = RLS-S2-012 approved starter. This is the EXACT first-frame camera placement, boots, ice-fishing hole, ice auger, frozen lake, snow shoreline and light. Preserve its geometry at 0.0s. Do NOT use Master Still as the opening.
IMAGE 2 / MASTER STILL = RLS-S2-012 final identity/reveal authority for ONE enormous realistic sturgeon under CLEAR BLUE LAKE ICE: elongated single connected body, long pointed snout, exactly four lower-jaw barbels, five longitudinal rows of bony scutes, naturally placed paired fins and ONE continuous tail. Use its fish anatomy, water color and lake scale at the later reveal. NOT an extra fish and NOT an ending-frame collage.

GLOBAL WORLD LOCK:
One continuous fully frozen mountain lake with a snow-covered tree line and distant winter mountains. Same hole and fishing gear, same boots, same camera position, same daylight and weather from beginning to end. Solid ice remains continuous EXCEPT the small previously drilled fishing hole. The fish remains UNDER the solid ice for the entire shot. No second species, no separate body, no breach. Under-ice visibility decreases naturally with distance and depth.

EIGHT BEATS / EXACT 15-SECOND TIMELINE:

BEAT 1 / 0.0–1.5s — FRAME ZERO HOOK
Start exactly from IMAGE 1. Static seated ice-fishing POV; two boots, drill hole and auger visible. Frozen lake is silent and apparently empty. Very subtle handheld breathing movement. Do NOT reveal the sturgeon at time zero.

BEAT 2 / 1.5–3.0s — UNUSUAL MOVEMENT
Far beneath the clear blue ice, ONE long faint low-contrast shadow slides slowly across the lakebed direction toward camera. Its boundary becomes gradually more defined; it is not a black smoke cloud or new hole in the ice. Camera shifts just a few degrees.

BEAT 3 / 3.0–4.5s — SCALE CLUE
The same shadow crosses closer to the fishing hole. Its continuous outline is longer than the nearby auger and boots provide as a scale reference. Fine suspended particles beneath the ice drift gently; ice itself stays still.

BEAT 4 / 4.5–6.5s — ARMORED BACK
Through naturally transparent blue ice, a section of ONE huge sturgeon's ridged armored back and bony scutes comes into focus. Movement is smooth, fish-like and continuous, not a rise through the ice. Camera tilts slightly to follow its travel.

BEAT 5 / 6.5–8.5s — ONE-FISH REVEAL
As the same single sturgeon passes near the fishing hole, reveal its elongated pointed head, correctly placed barbels, natural paired pectoral fins, broad torso and body connection. Preserve IMAGE 2 anatomy. The head passes under solid ice without touching the surface. Only one head, one connected torso, and one tail.

BEAT 6 / 8.5–10.5s — HAIRLINE CRACK

Thick lake ice is a stationary solid plane; the fish travels in WATER BELOW it, never through or on top of ice. Never spawn a second mouth, snout, fish, tail, hole or pair of boots.
